Bloom’s 1970 paper introduced hash coding with allowable errors.
A Bloom filter inserts a record by setting multiple hash-selected positions in a bit array.
When all positions selected for a query are set, a Bloom filter can report possible membership.
A nonmember can map only to bits already set by other inserted records and therefore produce a false positive.
The standard insertion-only Bloom-filter operation does not produce false negatives for inserted records.
For very small filters, including a 32-bit filter, approximate false-positive-rate predictions can have material error.
